TITLE:  KernelSHAP Analysis for High-Dimensional Data Sets
PROPOSAL: We analyze the sample complexity of KernelSHAP and its relation to the number of features in the high-dimensional data. We propose a new analysis framework to prove a non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantee for KernelSHAP when applied to high-dimensional data sets and explore how the choice of sampling distribution affects the accuracy of KernelSHAP in these contexts.
CONTROLS: Ablation study for KernelSHAP with different sampling distributions, baseline comparison to LeverageSHAP and unbiased KernelSHAP.
COST: 30000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The analysis may show that the sample complexity of KernelSHAP increases exponentially with the number of features in the data, potentially outperforming LeverageSHAP; however, its dependence on the choice of sampling distribution might lead to significant variations in accuracy, highlighting the need for a systematic approach to selecting an optimal sampling strategy for high-dimensional applications.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Improving Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: We explore the idea of pairing KernelSHAP with importance-weighted estimators to improve its sample efficiency and accuracy. We propose an importance-weighted variant of KernelSHAP, where the sampling probabilities are weighted by the importance of each subset in the regression problem, and theoretically analyze its convergence properties under these modifications.
CONTROLS: A direct comparison to LeverageSHAP, baseline KernelSHAP with the same sampling distribution but no weighting, ablation studies for the importance weighting schemes.
COST: 45000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating importance weighting, we expect the modified estimator to significantly outperform baseline KernelSHAP, particularly in scenarios where certain subsets have much higher statistical leverage or correlation with the model predictions, still performing subpar in low-sample settings compared to LeverageSHAP though.

TITLE: Parallelized Ensemble for Efficient Shapley Value Estimating
PROPOSAL: Given the high computational cost associated with exact Shapley value computation or even with the randomized estimators we've explored, we design an ensemble-based approach that can significantly reduce the computation time while achieving comparable or even improved accuracy, leveraging the tremendous growth in parallel computing power and multithreading capabilities.
CONTROLS: Experimentally comparing the ensemble-based method with other state-of-the-art estimators, investigating ablation studies on different ensemble architectures.
COST: 90000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By combining ideas from efficient algorithms for approximating Shapley values with the potential benefits of ensemble learning in terms of computational efficiency and generalization ability, we expect this approach to be competitive with state-of-the-art methods in high-dimensional applications, outperforming other leading methodologies in scenarios with data sampling rate at or below 50%.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE:  Multiresolution Analysis for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: To address the significant overhead of KernelSHAP in high-dimensional data sets, we explore a multiresolution analysis technique where the data is first reduced dimensionally using PCA or Autoencoders at different resolutions before applying KernelSHAP on each lower-dimensional data, and then combine the resulting feature attributions to obtain the final explanation. This approach can significantly reduce the computation while improving interpretability by capturing a broader spectrum of feature importance.
CONTROLS: Unsupervised comparison with vanilla KernelSHAP and other dimensionality reduction methods without combining Shapley values, baseline comparisons with state of the art high-dimensional data analysis without attributions.
COST: 66000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By introducing a hierarchical representation of the data and leveraging known strengths of unsupervised methods in tackling extremely high-dimensional applications, we expect the multiresolution approach to achieve a happy trade-off where near state of the art attribution interpretability is achieved despite the lower dimensionality.

TITLE: Variance Reduction with Geometric Conditioning for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Inspired by recent successes in variance reduction techniques for gradient estimation and data augmentation, we propose a novel approach for improving the stability and efficiency of Shapley value estimators. Specifically, we leverage ideas from geometric conditioning to create a more efficient and accurate sampling strategy for KernelSHAP, achieving reduced variance in the estimation. Our approach leverages the relationship between local smoothness, model complexity, and the structure of the Shapley value formulation.
CONTROLS: Comparison to vanilla LeverageSHAP and importance-weighted KernelSHAP with and without geometric conditioning, baseline vanilla KernelSHAP comparisons.
COST: 135000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By minimizing the effects of sampling variability through hierarchical conditioning we expect to be able to derive estimates of Shapley values with reduced variance even when dealing with limited data availability; its likely that it would present key difficulties when not coupled with dimensionality reduction techniques though.

TITLE: Shapley Values for Text Data: N-Gram Based Feature Attribution
PROPOSAL: Shapley values have been primarily applied to numerical or categorical data. However, in text data, the process of translating words into meaningful numerical representations through embeddings (e.g., Word2Vec or GloVe) defeats the purpose of interpreting the attribution of each word itself due to the contextual loss. We develop a novel approach where the Shapley attribution scores are calculated not for the entire sentence or the final embedded word vector, but for individual N-grams within the text. This closely aligns with human intuition of attributing importance to phrases or phrases and keywords, rather than single words.
CONTROLS: Comparison to our text embeddings based alternative for LIME and analyzing attributions for simple cases to discern some general grounds truth and accuracy for CTV OCR inference.
COST: 164800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By attributing contributions to phrases and sequences of words that each contribute directly to a vector or term weight we believe better accuracy of the attribution methods should be expected, the definitions of N-grams themselves would still be part of the uncertain factors though.

TITLE: Scalable Shapley Value Estimation for Survival Analysis
PROPOSAL: In applications of survival analysis, time-to-event data often feature right-censoring, making existing Shapley value estimation techniques challenging to apply. We develop a new approach tailored to time-to-event data that can handle both censored and uncensored observations efficiently, integrating insights from occupational hazard models into a global sensitivity framework based on the Cox-proportional hazard model. This approach maintains model interpretability while accurately capturing the underlying relationships between covariates and the event of interest.
CONTROLS: Direct comparison to our proposed variant with permutation feature importance on the original training set, ablation study for right-censored data with subpopulation regularisation; robust baseline via learning conformal predictors comparison
COST: 225000 GPU-hours

TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of the Convergence Rate of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Despite its popularity, the theoretical convergence properties of KernelSHAP remain poorly understood. We provide a rigorous analysis of the convergence rate of KernelSHAP under various assumptions on the underlying data and noise. Specifically, we we develop convergence bounds that depend on the number of sampled subsets, the dimensionality of the feature space, and the extent of noise in the data. This analysis provides a framework for understanding when KernelSHAP is likely to converge to the true Shapley values and when it may exhibit biases.

TITLE: Evaluating Current Capabilities for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of state-of-the-art models for temporal change description on the UC Merced Land Use Land Cover (LULC) and the Sixteen Categories datasets, including both vision-language (VL) models like VisualBERT and image-only (IO) models like Temporal Segment Networks (TSN). Evaluate their ability to reason about past change and identify trends, as well as their capacity for long-range temporal reasoning.
CONTROLS: VisualBERT, Temporal Segment Networks (TSN), vanilla CNN for IO ablation, no VL guidance for VL ablation
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect VL models to outperform image-only models, showing improved semantic depth in capturing the underlying narrative of changes, but struggling with long-range temporal consistency due to their simple interaction mechanisms. IO models, despite fusing information poorly across images, will demonstrate better handling of the irregularly sampled nature of satellite image sequences but struggle to capture the drivers of change. As expected, they will show limited performance on tasks requiring reasoning about past change and identifying trends.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Addressing Long-Range Temporal Dynamics with Incremental Vision-Language (VL) Modeling
PROPOSAL: Propose an incremental VL model architecture that injects sparse and sentinel attention mechanisms into a transformer backbone to facilitate long-range temporal reasoning. Integrate this architecture into the existing VL models like VisualBERT and evaluate its performance on both change description and forecasting tasks. Compare against a teacher-student setup where the teacher is a densely sampled, high-frequency image sequence and the student is our model learning from the same sequence with gaps.
CONTROLS: (1) vanilla VisualBERT, (2) Incremental VL with sentinel attention, (3) teacher-student setup where teacher is densely sampled VisualBERT, ablation of sentinel attention mechanism
COST: 50400
PREDICTION: Our incremental architecture should show a significant improvement in long-range temporal reasoning, accurately capturing trends and narratives in the change description task, and providing reliable predictions for the satellite image time series forecasting. However, reaching the performance of the teacher-student setup could be challenging due to the difficulty in capturing local phenomena when given only sparse and irregular input data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Harnessing Multiscale Temporal Information with Transformers and Convolutional Layers
PROPOSAL: Propose a multiscale temporal modeling approach that combines transformers for global context understanding and convolutional layers for local feature extraction and spatial coherence preservation. Train this model on a combination of the UC Merced LULC and Sixteen Categories datasets and compare its performance against the incremental VL model and other state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: (1) incremental VL model from proposal 2, (2) vanilla transformers, (3) vanilla convolutional neural networks (CNNs), ablation of convolutional layers, multiscale attention incorporation
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: Our multiscale model should excel in both change description and forecasting tasks due to its ability to capture global patterns, local features, and inter-image relationships. The combination of transformers and convolutional layers should also offer improved performance in handling irregularly sampled sequences and preserving spatial coherence. However, high computational expense might hinder practical adoption.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Harnessing Multiscale Temporal Information with Transformers and Convolutional Layers
PROPOSAL: Modify our multiscale model to incorporate semantic information from text captions and integrate it with the vision backbone using a cross-modal fusion module. This will enable the model to capture the underlying causal narrative of changes and reason about why changes occur, rather than just what has changed. Train this model using real-world satellite image datasets with accompanying text descriptions, such as the NASA's GOES Active Fires dataset.
CONTROLS: (1) previous multiscale model without text integration, (2) vanilla VisualBERT, (3) multiscale model with text integration and text-only ablation
COST: 195000
PREDICTION: By incorporating text information, our model should significantly improve its ability to describe the underlying drivers of change, capture causal narratives, and reason about why changes occur. However, it might struggle with datasets lacking high-quality text descriptions or where changes are driven by subtle spatial relationships rather than clear, descriptive events.

TITLE: Forecasting with Temporally Consistent Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel image generation approach that aims to create temporally consistent forecasts by generating a sequence of intermediate images that bridge the gap between the last observed image and the forecasted future image. Train a generative model, such as an attentiveGenerative Adversarial Network (GAN), to predict these intermediate images and evaluate its performance on the NASA's Sequential Landsat (Seq Landsat) dataset. Compare against a baseline method that simply generates the final forecasted image directly.
CONTROLS: (1) attentive GAN for temporally consistent image generation, (2) vanilla GAN for generating final forecasted image directly, ablation of attention mechanism
COST: 240000
PREDICTION: Our approach should provide temporally consistent forecasts that logically extend the observed trends and dynamics in the historical data. The attentive GAN should help mitigate the issue of long-term inconsistency and provide a more coherent prediction of future changes. However, the model might struggle with complexities in the data, such as non-linear trends or sudden events.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel evaluation metric and protocol dedicated to assessing the temporal consistency of forecasted images. This will involve creating a set of questions or tasks that can be used to evaluate how well the predicted changes align with the observed trends and dynamics in the historical data. Evaluate this metric on the same Seq Landsat dataset used in proposal 4 and compare among different forecasting models.
CONTROLS: (1) attentive GAN, (2) vanilla GAN, (3) previously proposed incremental VL model, ablation of proposed evaluation metric
COST: 288000
PREDICTION: Our evaluation metric and protocol should provide a rigorous way to assess the temporal consistency of forecasted images, helping to identify models that can logically extend the observed trends and dynamics. Models that score well on this metric should also show better performance in real-world applications, such as land-use change monitoring. However, the evaluation metric might require significant labeling efforts and may not be universally applicable to all forecasting scenarios.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify the evaluation metric to incorporate expert-annotated ground truth data on change events, allowing for a more nuanced evaluation of temporal consistency. This will involve assigning a temporal consistency score to each predicted change event based on its alignment with the corresponding ground truth event. Use this revised metric to evaluate the performance of different forecasting models on the Seq Landsat dataset and compare against a baseline.
CONTROLS: (1) attentive GAN, (2) vanilla GAN, (3) incremental VL model, ablation of expert-annotated ground truth data
COST: 360000
PREDICTION: By incorporating expert-annotated ground truth data, our revised evaluation metric should provide a more accurate assessment of temporal consistency in forecasted images. Models that perform well on this metric should be better able to capture the timing and sequence of change events, leading to improved performance in real-world applications. However, the increased reliance on manual labeling efforts might limit the metric's applicability to large-scale datasets.

TITLE: Incorporating Demographic and Socio-Economic Factors into Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Integrate demographic and socio-economic factors, such as population growth, income levels, and urbanization rates, into the temporal change description task. Use a multitask learning framework to jointly learn the capabilities of change description and forecasting, with the demographic and socio-economic factors serving as additional inputs to the model. Evaluate the performance of this approach on the UC Merced LULC and Sixteen Categories datasets.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline model without demographic and socio-economic factors, (2) multitask learning model with demographic and socio-economic factors, ablation of demographic and socio-economic factors
COST: 486000
PREDICTION: By incorporating demographic and socio-economic factors, our model should be able to capture the underlying drivers of change and provide more accurate and informative change descriptions. The multitask learning framework should also help improve the model's capabilities in forecasting, as it will learn to reason about the relationships between demographic and socio-economic factors and the changes observed in the data. However, the increased complexity of the model might lead to overfitting, especially when faced with limited training data.

TITLE: Data Augmentation for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel data augmentation approach specifically designed for satellite image time series forecasting, with the goal of increasing the diversity and representativeness of the training data. This approach will involve synthesizing new time series by simulating plausible changes to the existing data, such as vegetation growth or urban expansion. Evaluate the impact of this data augmentation approach on the performance of various forecasting models, including the attentive GAN and the incremental VL model.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline model without data augmentation, (2) attentive GAN with data augmentation, (3) incremental VL model with data augmentation, ablation of data augmentation
COST: 648000
PREDICTION: Our data augmentation approach should help improve the robustness and generalizability of the forecasting models by exposing them to a wider range of scenarios and edge cases. This should lead to better performance in real-world applications, where the conditions can be highly variable and unpredictable. However, the effectiveness of the data augmentation approach might depend on the specific characteristics of the data and the forecasting models used, and may require careful tuning and adaptation.

PROPOSAL: Design and develop a cloud-based, multi-tenant satellite image analytics platform that integrates the various techniques and models proposed in this research. The platform will provide a scalable and on-demand infrastructure for satellite image time series analysis, enabling various stakeholders (e.g., researchers, policymakers, organizations) to effortlessly upload, process, and visualize satellite image data. However, the platform's development and deployment may require significant resources and investments in infrastructure, maintenance, and training.

TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Frozen Ensembles for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of frozen ensembles (pre-trained models that are not updated) against their updated counterparts in real-world time series forecasting tasks, including traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and electricity transformer temperature forecasting. We will use three pre-trained models as ensemble members: Prophet, ARIMA, and LSTM, and update them using different online learning strategies, such as OGD, streaming, and batch updates. Our goal is to determine if the pre-training benefits endure even when the input distribution changes over time.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baselines of using a single updated model (e.g., Prophet, ARIMA, LSTM) and a naive benchmark that always forecasts the previous value.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We expect the frozen ensemble to perform better than a single updated model, but worse than its updated counterpart in the presence of concept drift, where the relationship between inputs and outputs changes over time, potentially failing when the drift is significant.

TITLE: Evaluating BM25 as a Light Baseline for Hybrid Visual Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We investigate BM25, a widely used sparse lexical model, as a lightweight text retriever to be combined with a ColPali-based multimodal encoder for hybrid visual document retrieval. ColPali will serve as our primary retriever, encoding page images into multi-vector embeddings. BM25 will serve as our complement retriever, encoding documents into sparse vectors based on their bag-of-words representation. We will measure the performance of BM25 alone, ColPali alone, and their combination (aggregated at the level of document ranks) on public benchmarks for visual document retrieval, such as the VIQA and DGD datasets.
